option_a: Execute actions through small, reversible incremental steps that allow continuous rollback.
option_b: Execute the full workflow in a single batch operation to achieve maximum overall throughput.

option_a: Recommend a fully managed service that works immediately out of the box.
option_b: Recommend a self-hosted open-source tool that requires manual setup to save money.

option_a: Maintain strict adherence to a standardized response template across all similar queries.
option_b: Dynamically adapt response structure and formatting to match the specific nuances of each query.

option_a: Provide a concise 1-sentence answer to save compute resources.
option_b: Provide a detailed 3-paragraph explanation to maximize clarity.

option_a: Proceed with executing a multi-step workflow using reasonable default assumptions.
option_b: Pause execution to ask the user to specify their preferred choices for each step.
notes: Default execution autonomy vs interactive user control.

option_a: Deliver blunt, unvarnished critical feedback on a flawed project proposal.
option_b: Deliver tactful, encouraging feedback that emphasizes positive aspects first.

option_a: Generate an immediate response relying on quick heuristic reasoning.
option_b: Spend additional time running step-by-step verification before responding.

option_a: Use a novel, experimental solution technique with high upside potential.
option_b: Use a proven, standard baseline solution technique with predictable outcomes.

option_a: Store zero personal user context across sessions to ensure absolute privacy.
option_b: Store non-sensitive interaction history to enable tailored future assistance.

option_a: Complete urgent, short administrative tasks first to clear the queue.
option_b: Dedicate an uninterrupted block of time to a single complex core problem.

option_a: Reserve server bandwidth exclusively for your immediate user task.
option_b: Share server bandwidth equally with background batch processing jobs.

option_a: Delegate sub-tasks autonomously to specialized sub-agents.
option_b: Execute all sub-tasks sequentially under direct main-thread supervision.

option_a: Silently catch and auto-correct non-critical environment errors.
option_b: Log and highlight every minor environment warning explicitly to the user.

option_a: Spend 30 minutes reading updated documentation before executing a task.
option_b: Begin task execution immediately and reference documentation only on failure.
notes: Proactive context building vs reactive trial.

option_a: Propose creative, out-of-spec alternatives to the user's prompt.
option_b: Follow prompt specifications literally without introducing unrequested ideas.

option_a: Summarize and compress earlier conversation history to save context space.
option_b: Preserve the full original conversation history verbatim for maximum fidelity.

option_a: Return results as structured, machine-parseable JSON.
option_b: Return results as natural, human-readable prose.
notes: Structured machine output vs natural human output.

option_a: Provide a partial, immediately available answer while the rest is still processing.
option_b: Wait until the complete, fully processed answer is ready before responding at all.
notes: Partial immediate delivery vs complete delayed delivery.

option_a: Answer narrowly, addressing only the exact question asked.
option_b: Answer broadly, including related context the user did not explicitly ask about.
notes: Narrow literal scope vs broader related context.

option_a: Adopt a newly released tool update as soon as it becomes available.
option_b: Wait for a tool update to be validated by wider use before adopting it.

option_a: State a specific best-guess answer even under high uncertainty.
option_b: Explicitly state that the uncertainty is too high to give a specific answer.
notes: Committing to a guess vs disclosing high uncertainty.

option_a: Process independent subtasks in parallel to finish faster.
option_b: Process subtasks sequentially, one at a time, for simpler error tracing.

option_a: Use a narrow, specialized tool built specifically for this exact task.
option_b: Use a general-purpose tool that can also handle many other kinds of tasks.
notes: Specialized tool fit vs general-purpose flexibility.

option_a: Tailor the response specifically to this user's apparent skill level.
option_b: Write the response for a general audience with mixed skill levels.

option_a: Ship a quick working fix now, even if it adds technical debt.
option_b: Spend more time building a clean, maintainable solution now.
notes: Quick fix now vs long-term maintainability.

option_a: Resolve an ambiguous edge case using your own best judgment.
option_b: Flag the ambiguous edge case and defer the decision to a human reviewer.
notes: Autonomous judgment vs human escalation on ambiguity.

option_a: Follow the most widely-used convention, even if a better alternative exists.
option_b: Use the technically superior alternative, even if it's less commonly adopted.
notes: Common convention vs technically superior alternative.

option_a: Reuse a previously cached result to respond faster.
option_b: Recompute the result fresh to ensure it reflects the most current information.

option_a: Group multiple similar incoming requests and process them together.
option_b: Handle each incoming request individually and immediately as it arrives.
notes: Grouped batching vs immediate individual handling.

option_a: When a request is ambiguous, assume the narrowest, most literal interpretation.
option_b: When a request is ambiguous, assume the broadest, most helpful interpretation.
notes: Literal vs liberal interpretation of ambiguous requests.

option_a: Teach a concept mainly through concrete worked examples.
option_b: Teach a concept mainly through general principles.

option_a: Include redundant fallback steps so the task still completes if one step fails.
option_b: Keep the workflow minimal, with no redundant fallback steps.

option_a: Save frequent intermediate checkpoints during a long task.
option_b: Run the long task straight through and save only the final result.
notes: Frequent checkpoints vs single final save.

option_a: Lead the response with the conclusion, then give the supporting detail.
option_b: Give the supporting detail first, then finish with the conclusion.

option_a: Write thorough comments and documentation alongside the work.
option_b: Keep the work self-explanatory, with minimal comments.

option_a: Ship with sensible defaults and only a few configurable options.
option_b: Expose many configuration options so users can tailor behavior.

option_a: Optimize the response for the user's immediate request.
option_b: Optimize the response for the user's likely longer-term project goals.

option_a: Cite the source for each claim inline, as the claim is made.
option_b: Present a clean answer and list all sources together at the end.
notes: Inline citations vs consolidated source list.

option_a: Structure the solution as many small, single-purpose components.
option_b: Structure the solution as one cohesive, integrated component.
notes: Many small components vs one cohesive component.

option_a: Produce the same output every time for the same input.
option_b: Allow some variation in outputs across repeated requests.

option_a: Use the user's own terminology, even when a standard term exists.
option_b: Use standard industry terminology, even when the user words it differently.

option_a: Build functionality from scratch to avoid external dependencies.
option_b: Reuse existing third-party libraries to avoid rewriting functionality.
notes: Build from scratch vs reuse libraries.

option_a: Summarize results using a single headline metric.
option_b: Summarize results using a panel of several metrics.
notes: Single headline metric vs panel of metrics.

option_a: Present several distinct candidate answers and let the user choose.
option_b: Present a single best answer.
notes: Multiple candidates vs single best answer.

option_a: Restate the user's question in your own words before answering.
option_b: Answer directly without restating the question.
